methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $16M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Roam Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Tim Swift, Mallory Ulaszek, and Saul Griffith, has raised $16.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics at Series B and Seed stages) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to $16M in total raised and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $33M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $1.8B. The peer set reflects the broader robotics sector maturity, where Bedrock and Dexterity trade at $1.8B and $1.6B respectively at Series B, while earlier-stage Walden sits at $1.1B.

The two methods produce a wide implied range of $28M to $1.9B, with a median of $841M. This disparity reflects fundamental uncertainty: the stage-progression method treats capital raised as a floor valuation anchor, while peer-median assumes Roam's growth trajectory and market position align with later-stage comparables. The gap highlights sensitivity to assumptions about capital efficiency, competitive positioning, and time-to-scale. Further diligence on revenue, customer traction, and technology defensibility relative to named peers would narrow this range materially.
